{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development / Hosting Agreement with HDI)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 5 compliant, 7 deviations and 6 rules for which no usable clause exists. The commercial architecture (30% revenue share on Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor, one-year auto-renewing term, mutual 90-day exit) is workable, and several rules are met outright — no MFN, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no employee non-solicit, and New York law with no arbitration clause. The Section 6.1 field-of-use restriction on us also sits at the playbook fallback and we are not redlining it.

The risk is concentrated in what the Agreement omits and in the exit economics. There is no IP ownership provision (HDI builds and hosts the Site and holds our Content and user data, yet ownership of deliverables and Company data is unallocated), no performance warranty, no vendor indemnity, no insurance obligation, no limitation of liability and no transition-assistance or data-return mechanic. Separately, Section 4.2(a)'s Termination Payment (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is an uncapped exit charge payable only by us and triggered by any Company termination, including termination for HDI's default; Section 6.1 exclusivity runs for a potentially perpetual term with no ongoing performance-based exit; Section 3.4 permits HDI records inspections with no frequency limit; and Section 10.3 lets HDI assign freely, including to a competitor.

Three redlines did not clear verification (Termination for Convenience, Audit, Limitation of Liability) and require manual drafting before the turn goes out.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Grant runs to "the Company" only, names no affiliates or contractors and no mechanism to add them, and is silent on revocability. Extend to affiliates and contractors, make non-revocable at will and transferable to a successor; affiliate coverage on prior written notice as fallback. | pass |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 6.1 restraint is limited to defined Deerskin Products and named comparators, confined to the internet channel, term-only with no post-term tail, and carved out by § 6.2 and § 8(b). Sits at the fallback; no redline. Absence of an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out noted only. | pass |
| Medium | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Exclusive dealing for a potentially perpetual auto-renewing term, with a Termination Payment on our exit and no performance-based release (§ 1.6 lapses at launch). Redline to fallback: confine to defined Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months, automatic release on HDI delivery or performance failure. § 6.3 reciprocal covenant left intact. | repaired |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | § 10.5 selects New York law with conflicts disclaimed (preferred); no arbitration clause. Only shortfall is the absence of an express exclusive New York County venue line — noted, not redlined. | pass |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No ownership provision; § 5.2 gives editorial control only and § 8 treats Content as confidential. Insert preferred clause: Company ownership/assignment of deliverables, HDI retains pre-existing IP with a perpetual royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, Company retains all rights in Company Data, no joint ownership. | repaired |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No MFN, benchmarking or matching mechanic; fees are a fixed revenue share under § 3.1. Meets preferred position. | pass |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Purely sales-based revenue share; the $11,000 monthly threshold is a floor in our favour, not a minimum spend. No multi-year lock-in. Termination Payment and exclusivity addressed under their own rules. | pass |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No hiring or solicitation restriction anywhere; employee references are limited to the confidentiality carve-out and independent-contractor clause. Meets preferred position. | pass |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | One-year renewals and no price-uplift mechanic are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Reduce the Company window to 30 days (60 days acceptable) while leaving HDI's 90 days intact; add a 60-day reminder and uplift cap. | repaired |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | § 4.1 notice mechanics sit at the fallback and are not redlined. The failure is § 4.2(a): an uncapped exit payment payable only by us and biting even on termination for HDI's default. Cap at three months' § 3.1 fees and carve out termination for HDI's breach and under § 1.6. | **fail — redline requires manual drafting** |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | § 9 covers only authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement; no services, conformance, legal-compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Insert new § 9(c) at preferred level (90-day workmanlike services, 12-month conformance, compliance with laws, no malicious code; repair, replacement or refund). No disclaimer present, so not "AS IS". | repaired |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Our assignment is unrestricted and HDI has no change-of-control termination right (both favourable). However § 10.3 has no consent standard, so HDI could assign to a competitor. Insert preferred consent standard with our affiliate/successor carve-out and confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment. | repaired |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | § 3.4 already gives 30 days' notice, business-hours access, payment-records-only scope and HDI-borne costs, but has no frequency limit. Add a once-per-12-month cap with an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor and no access to Company systems. Inspector identity and absence of a cost shift noted only. | **fail — redline requires manual drafting** |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere. Insert HDI indemnity as new § 9(c) (IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Content/Confidential Information/user data, gross negligence or wilful misconduct) with notice, control and cooperation; survives via § 10.7. No Company indemnity added; IP-only fallback offered. | repaired |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No insurance obligation, though HDI hosts the Site and holds user information and Company data under § 8.1. Insert new § 10.9: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. | pass |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | § 4.2 exit charge (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000) is a Customer-payable liquidated amount that can exceed a year of fees and is triggered by ordinary 90-day non-renewal. Delete; if unavoidable, cap at three months' fees. | repaired |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No cap, no exclusion of indirect damages; both parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages. Insert into § 9 (so it survives under § 10.7) a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and uncapped Excluded Claims. | **fail — redline requires manual drafting** |
| Low | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | § 4 covers only notice and the Termination Payment; no exit, migration, data-return or deletion right, although HDI operates the Site on its own server and holds our data. Insert new § 4.3: up to six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion. | repaired |

## Walk-away items

The following findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Exclusivity without a performance exit (§ 6.1 / § 4.1–4.2).** Exclusive dealing for the full, indefinitely renewing term with no service-level regime and no ongoing performance-based release. Must be capped at 12 months with automatic release on HDI delivery or performance failure.
2. **No HDI IP-infringement indemnity.** HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site and supplies the underlying software and technology; the total absence of any indemnity is unacceptable.
3. **No vendor insurance.** HDI processes user information and Company data under § 8.1; no coverage of any kind is a walk-away.
4. **Unlimited audit frequency (§ 3.4).** Inspections with no frequency cap are walk-away; the once-per-12-month limit is required.

We also treat the § 4.2(a) Termination Payment as a red-line-critical commercial item: as drafted it is uncapped, one-sided and payable even where we terminate for HDI's default.

## Next steps

1. **Manually draft the three unverified redlines** — T4C (§ 4.2(a) cap and breach carve-out), AUDIT (§ 3.4 frequency cap) and LOL-CAP (mutual cap into § 9) — before the turn is released; the automated edits did not verify.
2. **Confirm the insertions** for IP ownership, performance warranty (§ 9(c)), HDI indemnity (§ 9(c)), insurance (§ 10.9) and transition assistance (§ 4.3), and check that § 10.7 survival captures the new warranty, indemnity and liability provisions as intended.
3. **Brief the business** on the § 4.2 Termination Payment exposure at forecast Net Sales volumes so the negotiating team can price the exclusivity bargain against the exit cost.
4. **Confirm scope of use** for § 1.4 — identify which affiliates and contractors need access so the extended grant is drafted accurately.
5. **Hold as noted-only items** (raise only if the document is reopened): exclusive New York County venue, an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out to § 6.2, and a vendor renewal reminder mechanic.
6. **Send the turn** with the walk-away items flagged as gating, offering the stated fallbacks on exclusivity duration, renewal notice (60 days), indemnity (IP-only) and insurance limits."}
